app.name: Winch Up
app.tagline: Neighbors with winches, not a tow bill.

auth.signUpBody: You need an account to ask for a recovery.

account.title: Your account
account.body: Your details, what we tell you about, and who can see you.
account.emailHint: Contact an admin if you need this changed.
account.nameHint: What volunteers see when you're matched. No phone numbers or links.
account.regionHint: A town or county. Not your address.
account.notifyRecoveryHint: Requests near you, and updates on your own. Turning this off means you won't hear about a job.
account.notifyMarketingHint: Off unless you turn it on.
account.deleteBody: Gone for good: your sign-in, your profile, your phone number and name, your home location, and the exact spot of any recovery you filed.
account.deleteConfirm: This cannot be undone. You'll be signed out and your profile removed.

errors.active_job: You've accepted a job. Finish or hand it back first.
errors.not_signed_in: You're signed out. Sign in and try again.

account.vehiclesBody: What you drive, and what you can bring to a recovery.
account.deleteKept: Kept, with nobody's name on it: that each recovery happened and roughly where, the messages on it — a conversation belongs to two people — and posts other members replied to.
account.availableLabel: I can be called out to help someone
account.availableHint: Turn this on to get alerts when somebody near you is stuck. You can still browse requests and offer help with it off — nobody is ever obliged to go.
account.availableFailed: We could not save that. Try again.
account.notifyBody: Alerts, messages and which devices hear about them.
account.menuEquipmentHint: What you carry, and how far you'll drive
account.menuRecoveriesHint: Jobs you came out to, and your current one
account.menuTrailsHint: Browse trails and what people report
account.menuNotificationsHint: What reaches your phone, and which devices
account.menuResourcesHint: Gear, safety, etiquette, what to do first
account.loadFailed: We could not load your details. What you see below may not be what is saved — reload before changing anything.
account.menuBlockedHint: Who you have blocked, and how to undo it
account.menuLocationHint: Town, state and ZIP, for local events and offers
account.photoFailed: That photo did not upload. Try again.
account.photoTooMany: That is a lot of photos in one hour. Try again later.

vehicles.title: Your rigs
vehicles.body: What you drive, and what you can bring to a recovery.
vehicles.empty: No rigs yet. Add the one you'd bring.
vehicles.deleteConfirm: Remove {name}? This only affects your own list.
vehicles.recoveryPointsHint: Rated points you can pull from safely.
vehicles.winchCapacityHint: In pounds. Leave blank if you're not sure.
vehicles.equipmentHint: Only tick what's actually in the truck.

errors.load_failed: We couldn't load your rigs. Try again.
errors.save_failed: We couldn't save that. Try again.
errors.delete_failed: We couldn't remove that. Try again.
errors.primary_failed: We couldn't change your main rig. Try again.
errors.contact_in_notes: Notes can't contain a phone number or a link.
errors.too_many: That's the maximum number of rigs. Remove one first.

photo.label: Photo of your rig
photo.hint: Members see this on your profile. Taken outside, whole vehicle in frame, is ideal.
photo.failed: That photo would not upload. Try another one.

prompt.addPhoto: Add a photo of your rig so other members can see what you drive.
prompt.addRig: Add your rig, so members can see what you drive and what you can bring.

vehicles.showInCommunity: Show this rig on my profile
vehicles.showInCommunityHint: Other members see the rig and its photo. Your notes are never shown.

home.emergencyNote: If anyone is hurt, in water, or in traffic, call 911 first. We are volunteers, not emergency services.
home.how1: Tell us where you are and how you're stuck. Takes about two minutes.
home.how2: The nearest volunteers with the right gear are notified. The first one to answer takes it.
home.how3: You get their name and an ETA, and a link you can watch until you're out.
home.volunteerSoon: If you already pull people out in the Facebook groups, this is for you. We only call you out when someone near you needs the gear you actually have.
home.boardBody: The open board shows every request as it comes in, with the pin blurred and no phone numbers. Same as scrolling the group, without the notifications.
home.trailsBody: Where people run, what the ground was like last weekend, and whether you're allowed to be there — with a source for every claim about access.
home.resourcesTitle: What to carry, and how not to get hurt
home.resourcesBody: Checklists, what to do before you leave pavement, and the short list of things that hurt people during a recovery. Free, no account needed.

notFound.title: We couldn't find that
notFound.body: That link may have expired, or it was typed in slightly wrong. If you're stuck right now, start a new request.

join.title: Volunteer to help
join.intro: You already pull people out. This just puts it in front of you when someone near you needs it, instead of you scrolling the group hoping to catch a post in time.
join.phoneHint: We text you a code to confirm it. Call-outs themselves come through the app, and this number goes only to a driver whose job you take.
join.codeLabel: The code we just texted you
join.homeHint: A town or a cross street is plenty. We only use it to measure distance, and it is never shown to anyone.
join.homeFound: Found it — tap to look again
join.radiusHint: You will never get a call-out further than this.
join.equipmentHint: Pick everything you actually have. We only send you jobs your gear can handle.
join.vehicleDescHint: This is what the stranded driver sees, so they know who pulled up. No phone numbers or links.
join.availableLabel: I can be called out to help someone
join.availableHint: This is what puts you in the alerts for recoveries near you, once an admin has approved you. You can turn it off any time in your account settings.
join.nightHint: Turn this off and we will leave you alone between 9pm and 6am.
join.waiver: I have read and accept the <link>volunteer agreement</link>.
join.pendingBody: An admin checks every signup before anyone starts getting call-outs. It is how we keep tow companies out of a volunteer group. Your dashboard says so once you are approved.

errors.invalid_phone: That doesn't look like a US mobile number.
errors.otp_send_failed: We couldn't send the code. Check the number and try again.
errors.bad_code: That code didn't work. Check it or ask for a new one.
errors.address_not_found: We couldn't find that place. Try a town and state.
errors.save_failed: Something broke on our end. Try again.

errors.not_signed_in: Your session expired. Confirm your number again.
errors.phone_required: Please verify a mobile number to finish signing up. Volunteers are reached by text when somebody nearby needs help.
errors.phone_taken: That number is already on another account. Sign in with that account, or contact us at help@winch-up.com so we can sort it out.

join.smsConsent: By giving us your number you agree to receive text messages from Winch Up: a code to confirm this number, and call-outs when somebody needs recovery help near you. Message frequency varies. Message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out, HELP for help. See our Terms and Privacy Policy.

me.signedOutTitle: Sign in to see your jobs

me.notApproved: This account isn't approved for call-outs. Contact the group admins if you think that's wrong.
me.onCallHint: Call-outs show up here and in your notifications when someone nearby needs your gear.
me.pausedHint: No call-outs until you turn this back on.
me.approximate: approximate pin until you take it

errors.server_error: Something broke on our end. Try again.

errors.not_approved: You aren't approved for call-outs yet.
errors.wrong_status: That job isn't in a state where you can do that.
errors.no_open_offer: There's no open offer to answer.

location.title: Where you are right now
location.body: By default we match you from your home address. If you're already out on the trail, share where you actually are and you'll be matched from there instead.
location.note: One position, stored when you press the button. Nothing runs in the background and nothing tracks you. It's ignored after a couple of hours and we go back to your home address.

errors.denied: Your browser blocked location. You'll need to allow it in browser settings.
errors.unavailable: We couldn't get a position. Try again outside or with a better signal.
errors.unsupported: This browser can't share a location.
errors.too_inaccurate: That position was too vague to use. Try again outside.
errors.not_a_responder: You're not signed up as a volunteer yet.

me.equipmentAck: I have the gear this needs and I can do it safely
me.unverifiedBody: An admin has not checked your profile. That does not stop you helping anyone — it just means your offers do not carry a verified badge yet.
me.myRequestOffers: {count, plural, one {# volunteer has offered — pick one} other {# volunteers have offered — pick one}}
me.accountSettingsHint: Your rigs, alerts, password and phone

board.title: Open board
board.subtitle: Every request as it comes in. Same as watching the group, without the notifications.
board.privacyNote: Pins on this page are moved about {miles} mile from the real spot, and no phone numbers or names are shown. Exact locations only go to the volunteer who takes the job.
board.approxArea: Open the approximate area in maps
board.mapUnavailable: The map is not set up yet. The list shows the same requests.

help.title: Help someone
help.subtitle: Open recovery requests near you. If you can safely help, offer.
help.privacyNote: Locations here are approximate, to about a mile. The exact spot and a way to reach them are shared only with the person the driver picks.
help.empty: Nothing open near you right now. That is a good sign.
help.alreadyOffered: Your offer is in. The driver chooses who comes out.
help.safetyPrompt: Only offer if you can get there and do this safely. You can turn back at any point, and nobody is obliged to go.
help.equipmentAck: I have the gear this needs and I can do it safely
help.etaLabel: How long to get there? (minutes, optional)
help.etaInvalid: Give a number of minutes between 1 and 600, or leave it blank.
help.noteHint: No phone numbers or links. You can talk directly once they pick you.

errors.already_covered: Someone else has already been picked for this one.
errors.no_recovery_profile: We could not set up your helper profile. Try again.
errors.equipment_not_acknowledged: Confirm you have the gear and can do this safely.
errors.offer_not_possible: You cannot offer on this one any more.
errors.no_open_offer: You do not have an open offer on this one.
errors.membership_agreement_required: You need to sign the membership agreement before you can do this. It only takes a minute.

help.photosUnavailable: Photos are not available for this request.

post.title: Post this to the group
post.intro: Formatted the way the group admins already ask for. Copy it, paste it, attach the photos.
post.noAutoPost: Facebook shut down the Groups API, so nothing here can post for you. Copy and paste is the whole trick.
post.copied: Copied — paste it into the group
post.attachPhotosHint: Save these and attach them to the post. The text does not carry images.
post.photoLinksExpire: These links expire in ten minutes. Reload the page for fresh ones.

signin.title: Admin sign in
signin.notAdmin: That number is signed in, but it isn't an admin.

errors.send_failed: We couldn't send a code to that number.

dashboard.pickVolunteer: Text or assign a volunteer directly. Assigning skips the ring and hands them the job.
dashboard.noVolunteers: No free volunteers on call right now.
dashboard.cancelConfirm: Cancel {code}? The person who asked for help will see the search stop, and any volunteer already on the way is texted that the job is off. This cannot be undone.
dashboard.noteTexted: Texted them, and added the offer to this recovery.
dashboard.noteResent: Sent them another text. They already had the offer, so nothing else changed.

noteNoText.no_sms_consent: Added the offer — they get it by push and in the app. No text was sent, because they have not agreed to recovery texts.
noteNoText.stopped: Added the offer — they get it by push and in the app. No text was sent, because they replied STOP.
noteNoText.no_phone: Added the offer — they get it by push and in the app. No text was sent, because we have no number for them.

err.failed: That did not work. Try again, and tell somebody if it keeps happening.
err.not_found: That recovery no longer exists. Refresh the queue.
err.no_responder: That volunteer no longer exists. Refresh the queue.
err.not_approved: Nobody has approved that volunteer yet, so they cannot be called out. Approve them under Volunteers first.
err.already_closed: That recovery is already closed — somebody may have just finished it.
err.forbidden: You do not have permission to do that.
err.mfa_required: This needs a second factor. Sign out and sign in again at the main sign-in page, which asks for your code.
err.signed_out: You have been signed out. Sign in again.
err.no_result: No answer came back. Refresh the queue and check whether it happened.

responders.reasonPlaceholder: Reason (kept on file, shown to nobody)

settings.dispatchHint: Values are JSON. Ring radii are an array of miles; the rest are numbers or true/false.
settings.proHint: Shown to a requester only when nobody has volunteered after the full escalation window.
settings.legalWarning: Publishing creates a new version. It never edits what people have already agreed to — that is what makes the waiver record worth anything.
settings.legalBothRequired: Both languages are required. A missing translation means somebody agrees to something they cannot read.
settings.blockHint: A blocked number can't create requests or sign up as a volunteer.

intake.intro: For when someone posts in the group instead of using the site. This creates a real request and starts the normal dispatch.
intake.pastedHint: Kept as the public notes, trimmed to 500 characters. Take out phone numbers.
intake.locationHint: Coordinates, a Google Maps link, or a what3words address.
intake.badPhone: That isn't a US mobile number.
intake.consentWarning: You are creating this on someone else's behalf. Make sure you have actually spoken to them, that nobody is hurt, and that they know volunteers are coming.
intake.createdBody: Volunteers will start getting texts on the next tick.

incidents.title: Safety reports
incidents.body: What people told us went wrong. The person a report is about never sees it.
incidents.urgent: Money, injury or harassment. Deal with this before the rest.
incidents.subject: About
incidents.banHint: To stop them being dispatched, set them to banned on the Volunteers tab.

security.title: Two-step sign in
security.body: An admin account can read every requester's phone number and exact location, approve volunteers, ban people and change the waiver everyone has agreed to. A password on its own is thin protection for that.
security.noFactors: You haven't set one up yet.
security.scanIt: Scan this with Google Authenticator, 1Password, Authy — any of them.
security.orTypeIt: Can't scan? Type this in instead:
security.qrAlt: QR code for your authenticator app
security.codeLabel: The six digits from the app
security.enrolledNote: Set up. Sign out and back in once, then you can require it for everyone.
security.enforcementBody: When this is on, every admin action needs a code — not just signing in. Reading the queue, approving a volunteer, all of it.
security.adminsCovered: {with} of {total} admins have an authenticator set up.
security.enforcementOn: On. Admin actions need a code.
security.enforcementOff: Off. A password is all anyone needs right now.
security.enrolFirst: Set up your own authenticator first — otherwise turning this on locks you out.
security.signInAgainFirst: Sign out and back in with your code first, so we know it works.

errors.enrol_and_sign_in_first: Sign out and back in with your code first. We won't switch this on from a session that hasn't used it.
errors.no_admin_has_mfa: No admin has an authenticator yet. Turning this on would lock everyone out.
errors.bad_code: That code didn't work. Check the app and try the current one.
errors.challenge_failed: We couldn't start the check. Try again.
errors.enrol_failed: We couldn't set that up. Try again.

system.title: Is anything running?
system.body: An idle system and a dead one look the same from every other screen. This is where they don't.
system.stalledSince: Last ran {when}. Nothing is being dispatched — requests won't escalate and no volunteer is being notified.
system.neverRan: It has never run. Nothing is being dispatched.
system.stalledWhatToDo: Check the pg_cron job in Supabase, and that the Edge Function still has the right secret.
system.noneReachable: No volunteer can be reached right now. A request would escalate through every ring and find nobody.

trails.title: Trails
trails.body: Nothing goes up without a source for whether it's open, and publishing puts your name on it.
trails.name: Name
trails.accessSourceHint: Something a person could check: "county GIS map, 22 Sep 2026", "park website", "owner gave the group permission by phone".
trails.difficultySourceHint: "Group admins", "park signage". It's an opinion; say whose.
trails.statusHint: Publishing records you as the person who checked it.
trails.conditionCount: {count, plural, =0 {No member reports} one {# member report} other {# member reports}}

errors.access_source_required: Say where the access claim came from.
errors.bad_slug: Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens only.
errors.slug_taken: Another trail already uses that URL name.
errors.bad_enum: One of those values isn't valid.

ads.title: Advertising
ads.body: Three separate decisions: is the business real, should the campaign run where it says, and should these exact words sit next to this group's name.
ads.rule1: Nothing may imply that a paid advertiser is safer, better qualified or more reliable than a volunteer.
ads.rule2: Nothing may suggest that paying gets a faster recovery, or any priority at all.
ads.rule3: A recovery or towing advertiser carries the extra line automatically. Check it reads honestly with their copy.
ads.verificationHint: A sentence somebody could be held to: "LLC registered in Texas, phone answered, address matches the yard".
ads.verificationRequired: An approval needs this. A green tick on its own is not a check.
ads.towingWarning: Recovery or towing. This is the category where a reader mistaking an advertiser for a volunteer costs them money at the roadside. Read the copy carefully.
ads.notAVolunteerPreview: This is a paid advertiser, not a Winch Up volunteer. They charge for recovery. Winch Up volunteers never do.

errors.verification_note_required: Say what you checked before approving.

mfa.title: One more step
mfa.why: Admin accounts need their authenticator code each time they sign in. This session was signed in without it.
mfa.what: Nothing is wrong with your account. Sign out and sign in again, and you will be asked for the six-digit code from your authenticator app.
mfa.signOutAndIn: Sign out and sign in again

alerts.title: Recovery alerts
alerts.smsOff: Outbound SMS is switched off, so call-outs are recorded but not sent. Volunteers are still alerted by push and in-app. Turn on sms.outbound_enabled in Settings to start texting.
alerts.medianNote: Median reply: {median}. The median is the more honest number when one volunteer answers hours late.
alerts.noWaves: No waves have opened in this window.
alerts.settingsNote: Read-only here. Change them in Settings, where every setting lives.

emergency.heading: Is anyone hurt or in danger?
emergency.body: Call 911 first. We are volunteers, not emergency services. If your vehicle is in water, in a traffic lane, or on fire, get out and call 911 now.
emergency.acknowledge: Nobody is hurt or in danger. Keep going.

location.outsideArea: That looks like it's outside our area. Double-check the pin before you send.
location.locating: Finding you… hold still for a few seconds.
location.denied: Your phone blocked location access. Use the map or paste a link instead, or turn location on in your browser settings.
location.unavailable: We couldn't get a GPS fix. Use the map or paste a link instead.
location.weakFix: That fix is rough. If you can, wait a few seconds or set it on the map.
location.mapHelp: Move the map until the pin is on your vehicle.
location.mapLabel: Map. Pan to place the pin.
location.mapUnavailable: The map couldn't load. Paste coordinates or a Google Maps link instead.
location.pasteHint: Coordinates, a Google Maps link, or a what3words address.

pasteError.unrecognised: We couldn't read that. Try coordinates like 29.7604, -95.3698.
pasteError.short_link_no_coords: That short link didn't contain a location. Open it, then copy the full link.
pasteError.short_link_failed: We couldn't open that link. Try the full Google Maps link.
pasteError.w3w_unavailable: We can't look up what3words addresses yet. Use GPS or the map instead.
pasteError.w3w_not_found: That what3words address didn't match a place.
pasteError.w3w_failed: The what3words lookup failed. Use GPS or the map instead.
pasteError.network: No connection. Try again in a moment.

location.noteLabel: Anything that helps us find you
location.noteHint: Optional. Gate, road name, landmark, which side of the creek.
location.notePlaceholder: Past the second cattle gate, blue tractor at the turn
location.mapHelpFull: Drag the map, tap a spot, or drag the pin. Satellite shows the treeline and the crossings — a street map out here is a grey line through nothing.

photos.help: A photo tells a volunteer whether to bring a winch or a tractor. Optional, but it helps a lot.
photos.failed: That photo didn't upload. You can try again or keep going without it.
photos.privacy: Photos are shrunk on your phone and stripped of location data before they're sent.

situation.depthHint: Roughly where does it come up to?
situation.needsTractorHint: Pick this if a truck alone won't do it.
situation.needsSecondTruck: Going to need a second truck
situation.needsSecondTruckHint: Heavy vehicle, or a bad angle.
situation.notesHint: Optional. Shown publicly, so no phone numbers or links.
situation.notesPlaceholder: Back end dropped into a rut after the rain. Tires just spin.

land.permissionHint: Volunteers won't come onto private land without it.

contact.phoneHint: So the volunteer who comes out can call you. Your status page opens as soon as you send this.
contact.privacy: Your number is never shown publicly. It goes only to the volunteer who takes your request.

consent.photoCount: {count, plural, =0 {No photos} one {# photo} other {# photos}}
consent.waiver: I have read and accept the <link>waiver</link>.
consent.rules: I have read and accept the <link>ground rules</link>.

errors.invalid_phone: That doesn't look like a US mobile number.
errors.invalid_location: We don't have a usable location yet. Go back a step.
errors.blocked: This number can't create requests. Contact the group admins.
errors.rate_limited_phone: That number has already sent several requests today. If this is an emergency, call 911.
errors.rate_limited_ip: Too many requests from this connection. Wait a few minutes and try again.
errors.server_error: Something broke on our end. Try again — your answers are saved.
errors.validation_failed: Something in the form isn't right. Go back and check.
errors.contact_info_not_allowed: Take the phone number or link out — this part is shown publicly.
errors.account_required: You need an account to send a request. Sign in and we'll bring you back here.
errors.membership_agreement_required: You need to sign the membership agreement before you can do this. It only takes a minute.

headline.submitted: We've got your request and we're lining up volunteers.
headline.dispatching: We're notifying volunteers near you. Keep this page open.
headline.unmatched: Nobody has taken it yet. Here are some paid options while we keep trying.
headline.accepted: A volunteer is on the way. Stay with your vehicle if it's safe.
headline.on_site: Your volunteer says they're on site.
headline.expired: This request was closed with no answer.

status.notifying: {count, plural, =0 {Looking for volunteers within {miles} miles} one {# volunteer notified within {miles} miles} other {# volunteers notified within {miles} miles}}
status.unmatchedBody: We've called out to everyone in range. We're still trying, but if you can't wait, these operators charge for recovery.
status.noProOptions: No paid operators have been added for your area yet.
status.cancelConfirm: Cancel this request? Volunteers heading your way will be told to stop.
status.thankYouHint: We'll pass this to the volunteer. No phone numbers or links.
status.autoRefresh: This page updates itself every {seconds} seconds.

errors.server_error: Something broke on our end. Try again.
errors.contact_info_in_note: Take the phone number or link out of your note.
errors.no_responder: Nobody has accepted this request yet.

status.offersTitle: {count, plural, one {# volunteer has offered} other {# volunteers have offered}}
status.offersBody: Pick whoever suits you best. Nobody is on their way until you choose.
status.offersPrivacyNote: When you pick someone, they get your name, your number and your exact location, and you get theirs. The others are told it is covered.
status.awaitingChoiceBody: Pick who comes out. Nobody is on their way until you do.
status.offersMoreTitle: {count, plural, one {# more volunteer has offered} other {# more volunteers have offered}}
status.offersMoreBody: Somebody is already coming. If you need a second rig — a tractor as well as a winch — you can add them to the team.
status.offersMorePrivacyNote: Anyone you add gets your name, your number and your exact location, the same as the first.

report.title: Report what happened
report.body: This goes to the admins. The person you're reporting never sees it, and never finds out who reported them.
report.whatHappenedHint: What happened, when, and anything that would help us act on it. Phone numbers are fine here — only admins read this.
report.thanksBody: An admin will look at it. We won't tell them who reported it.

errors.description_too_short: Tell us a little more — at least a sentence.
errors.description_too_long: That's too long. Keep it under 2000 characters.
errors.not_signed_in: You're signed out. Sign in and try again.
errors.rate_limited: You've sent several reports today. Contact an admin directly.
errors.server_error: Something broke on our end. Try again.

thread.title: Messages
thread.privateNote: Everyone on this recovery can read this — you and whoever is helping. Nobody else can, including anyone you shared the status link with.
thread.empty: Nothing yet. Say where you are, or what the ground is like.
thread.placeholder: Gate code is 4412, blue Tacoma past the cattle guard…
thread.closedNote: This recovery is finished, so messages are closed. If something went wrong, use the report link below.
thread.waitingNote: Held on this phone until there is signal. It sends itself — you don't have to retype it.
thread.queuedCount: {count, plural, one {# message waiting to send} other {# messages waiting to send}}
thread.offline: No connection. Anything you send is held here until there is.
thread.locationPrivate: Only people on this recovery can see this.

errors.too_long: That's too long. Keep it under 2000 characters.

legal.privacyBody:
Winch Up is a volunteer off-road vehicle recovery dispatcher operating in Texas, operated by {entity}.

WHAT WE COLLECT

When you ask for help: your name, your mobile number, the location of your vehicle, photographs you choose to upload, and details about the vehicle and the situation.

When you volunteer: your name, your mobile number, the area you are willing to travel to, and the equipment and vehicle you have.

For everyone: the email address and password you sign in with, and basic technical records such as the IP address a request was filed from, which we use to prevent abuse.

HOW WE USE IT

Your mobile number is used to confirm it belongs to you, and to send you messages about recoveries you are involved in. A requester's number and exact location are released only to a volunteer who has taken their recovery — not to the public board, and not to volunteers who were notified but did not take it.

Photographs have their location data removed in your browser before they are uploaded.

WHAT WE DO NOT DO

We do not sell or share your SMS opt-in data or personal information with third parties for marketing purposes.

We do not sell your personal information. We do not use your location to track you: a position is recorded when you share one, and is used to match you to nearby recoveries.

TEXT MESSAGES

Volunteers who confirm a mobile number receive texts about recovery requests near them. Reply STOP at any time to stop receiving them, or HELP for help. Message and data rates may apply. Message frequency varies.

KEEPING AND DELETING

Closed recoveries have the phone number and exact location removed after a retention period. Deleting your account removes your name, number, saved locations and shared positions.

CONTACT

{entity}
help@winch-up.com
legal.smsTermsBody:
{entity}, trading as Winch Up, sends text messages to volunteers who have signed up and confirmed a mobile number.

WHAT WE SEND. A one-time code to confirm your number, and call-outs when somebody needs recovery help near you. Message frequency varies and depends on how many recoveries happen in your area.

COST. Message and data rates may apply. Winch Up does not charge for these messages; your mobile carrier may.

HOW TO STOP. Reply STOP to any message to stop receiving them. You will get one confirmation and nothing after that. Reply START to begin again.

HELP. Reply HELP for help, or email help@winch-up.com.

CARRIERS. Mobile carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages.

Spanish speakers may reply BAJA to stop and AYUDA for help.

resources.title: Getting out, and not needing to
resources.intro: What to carry, what to check before you leave pavement, and how a recovery goes wrong. Written by people who pull each other out, not by instructors.
resources.notProsBody: Nobody here is a certified recovery operator, a mechanic or a medic unless they tell you they are, and we do not check. This is what the group has learned, offered freely. It is not training, not a standard, and not a substitute for hiring somebody who does this for a living.
resources.emergencyTitle: If somebody is hurt, call 911 first.
resources.emergencyBody: Injury, a vehicle in moving water, or anything in a traffic lane is an emergency call, not a recovery request. We are volunteers with trucks. Nobody is on shift and nobody is obliged to come.

gear.title: What to carry
gear.blurb: The things that turn a bad afternoon into an inconvenience.
gear.lede: None of this makes a recovery safe by itself. A rated shackle on a truck with nowhere rated to hook it is still nowhere to hook it.

sections.heading: Always in the truck
items: A full-size spare that holds air, and the tools to actually change it — including a breaker bar if your lug nuts were put on by a shop.
A tyre plug kit and a way to put air back in. Most trail punctures are sidewall-survivable and plug fine.
Jumper cables or a jump pack.
A jack that works on soft ground, and a flat board to stand it on. A bottle jack on mud is a jack in the mud.
More water than you think. The person coming to get you will want some too.
A torch that is not your phone, and spare batteries.
A first aid kit you have opened before today.

sections.heading: Before you leave pavement
items: A tyre deflator and a gauge. Airing down is the cheapest traction there is.
A compressor, because airing down is a one-way trip without one.
Traction boards. They get more vehicles out than winches do.
Gloves. Every recovery involves picking up something you would rather not.
A charger that runs off the truck, not a power bank you charged last week.
A shovel. Often the whole recovery.

sections.heading: If you are the one doing the pulling
items: A kinetic rope or recovery strap rated well above the weight of the heavier vehicle.
Soft shackles, or rated bow shackles. Not hardware-store clevises.
A damper for every line that goes under load — a purpose-made one, or a heavy wet blanket or jacket.
A tree strap if you might anchor to a tree, so you do not ring-bark it and so the tree survives to be an anchor next time.
A second person who knows what is about to happen.

sections.heading: Never pull from these
items: A tow ball. It shears under a snatch load and becomes a projectile that goes through a windscreen. This is the one that kills people.
A hitch pin through an empty receiver. Use a rated shackle mount.
Chains with hooks. No stretch, and the hook goes somewhere when it lets go.
Ratchet straps and cargo straps. They are for holding things still.
The little tie-down loops used to strap a vehicle to a trailer. They are rated for holding a parked car, not for pulling a stuck one.
Suspension arms, steering components, bumpers that are not bolted to the frame, or a tow hook that came with the truck unless you know what it is rated for.

before.title: Before you go
before.blurb: Five minutes at home that decide how the night goes.
before.lede: Most long recoveries are long because of something that was decided before anyone left the house.

sections.heading: Tell a person, not a group
items: Where you are going, roughly which way, and when you will be back.
When they should start making calls. An hour late is different from four hours late, and they cannot judge that unless you tell them.
A post in a group is not this. A person expecting you is this.

sections.heading: Assume there is no signal
items: Download the offline map for the area before you leave the house.
Screenshot the map, so you have it when the app cannot load tiles.
Write the coordinates of where you are headed on paper. A phone that dies takes the whole plan with it.

sections.heading: Fuel, water, daylight
items: Half a tank is the turn-around point, not the worry point.
Work out when it gets dark, then subtract an hour.
Water for everyone in the vehicle, plus some for whoever comes out to you.

sections.heading: Air down, and plan to air up
items: Lower pressure is the cheapest traction there is, and it is free.
Know the pressure you are going to, and check it rather than guessing.
You need a compressor to get home. Borrowing one at the gate is not a plan.

sections.heading: Go with somebody
items: A second vehicle is the difference between an inconvenience and a night out.
If you are going alone, tell somebody the route and stick to it.

safety.title: Doing a recovery without hurting anyone
safety.blurb: The short list of things that actually hurt people.
safety.lede: This is not training. It is what the group has learned, and some of it was learned badly. If you have not done this before, go with somebody who has and watch first.

sections.heading: Before anything goes under load
items: Agree who is in charge. One person calls it, everybody else does what they say.
Agree who can call a stop. Everybody can call a stop.
Walk the line the pull will take, and decide where people will stand — which is not in it and not beside it.
Send bystanders behind a vehicle, well back. Phones too. A recording of somebody being hurt is still somebody being hurt.

sections.heading: A line under tension is stored energy
items: A kinetic rope is designed to stretch. What it stores comes back along the line, fast, if anything lets go.
Put a damper over every line under load. A heavy wet blanket works. It drops the line instead of letting it fly.
Stay out of the arc, not just out of the line. Things that let go go sideways.
Check both ends before every attempt. Most failures are at the attachment, not in the middle.

sections.heading: Hook to something rated
items: Rated recovery points, bolted to the frame, on both vehicles.
If there is nowhere rated to hook, that is the end of the attempt. It is not a reason to use something else.
See the list of what never to pull from in the gear guide. The tow ball is the one that kills people.

sections.heading: Go slow, stop often
items: Short attempts with a look at everything in between beats one big one.
If the stuck vehicle has not moved in three tries, change something — dig, air down further, change the angle — rather than pulling harder.
Nothing good has ever come from a running start nobody was sure about.

sections.heading: Know when to stop
items: It is dark and nobody planned for dark.
The water is coming up.
Somebody is hurt, cold, overheating or frightened.
Nobody is sure what to do next and people are starting to guess.
The vehicle keeps until morning. Everything about this gets easier in daylight, and a stuck truck is worth less than the people standing around it.

sections.heading: If somebody is hurt
items: Stop the recovery. Everything stops.
Call 911. Give coordinates, not landmarks.
We are volunteers with trucks. We are not medics, and nobody here is trained to decide whether an injury is serious.

etiquette.title: Trail etiquette
etiquette.lede: Nearly every closed trail in Texas was closed because of something somebody did, not because of the land itself.

sections.heading: Permission is per-visit
items: Private land means the owner's word, this time, for you.
Somebody else having had permission is not permission. Neither is having been there before.
If you cannot say who gave you permission, you do not have it.

sections.heading: Gates as you found them
items: Open stays open. Closed stays closed. Latched stays latched.
If you find a gate you cannot work out, turn around.

sections.heading: Stay on the line
items: No cutting corners, and no new line around an obstacle. The bypass becomes the trail, and then the trail is twice as wide.
Driving around a mudhole is how mudholes become fifty feet across.
If the trail is too wet to drive without widening it, it is too wet.

sections.heading: Leave it better
items: Pack out what you brought, and some of what you did not.
Fill the ruts you cut if you can.
Do not leave recovery gear, straps or boards behind. Somebody will, and it will be blamed on all of us.

sections.heading: Around other people
items: Yield to anything coming uphill, and to anyone on foot, on a bike or on a horse. Stop and turn the engine down for horses.
Slow and quiet near houses, camps and stock.
Do not block a gate, a turnaround or a narrow spot while you sort yourself out.

sections.heading: If you break something, say so
items: A broken gate that gets reported is a gate that gets fixed.
A broken gate that gets found is a trail that gets closed.

stuck.title: When you are the one stuck
stuck.blurb: What to do first, and what happens after you ask.
stuck.lede: Being stuck is usually boring and occasionally dangerous. The first job is working out which one this is.

sections.heading: Call 911 first if
items: Anybody is hurt.
The vehicle is in moving water, or water is rising.
You are in a traffic lane or anywhere a vehicle could hit you.
You cannot stay warm enough, or cool enough, to wait several hours.
Winch Up is volunteers. Nobody is on shift, nobody is obliged to come, and nobody here is an emergency service.

sections.heading: Get your location into a form somebody else can use
items: The request page takes it from your phone, and shows you how accurate it is.
On a borrowed phone, read the coordinates out of a maps app and type them in.
A dropped pin you cannot describe out loud is not a location. Numbers are.

sections.heading: Make the phone last
items: Brightness down, data off between messages, nothing streaming.
One charged phone is worth more than three flat ones — pick one and put the others away.
Send the important message before the battery gets interesting.

sections.heading: Stay with the vehicle
items: It is far easier to find than you are.
It is shelter, and it has lights.
Walking out in the dark in unfamiliar country is how a recovery becomes a search.

sections.heading: What happens after you send a request
items: Volunteers near you are told what you need and how far away you are — not your phone number.
The first one to answer takes it. Nobody is dispatched; they are choosing to drive out.
You get their first name, their vehicle and an ETA, and a link you can watch and share.
If nobody answers within about twenty-five minutes, we tell you, and we show you paid operators instead. That is not a failure of yours.

sections.heading: Nobody charges you
items: No money changes hands for a Winch Up recovery. Not a fee, not a tip, not fuel money asked for on the spot.
If somebody asks you for money, that is not how this works. Report it, and we will deal with it.
Buying somebody a meal afterwards because you want to is your business.

weather.title: Weather and conditions
weather.blurb: The two things that change a Texas trail overnight: water and heat.
weather.lede: A road that was fine at nine in the morning can be un-driveable at four in the afternoon and fine again the next day. Check before you leave, not when you get there.

sections.heading: Turn around, don't drown
items: Most flood deaths in Texas happen in vehicles, at crossings people had driven a hundred times.
A foot of moving water will float most trucks. Two feet will move them.
You cannot see whether the road is still under the water, and low-water crossings wash out from underneath.
If water is over the road, the day is over. Wait or go around.

sections.heading: Clay and caliche change completely when wet
items: Black clay goes from grippy to greasy in one shower, and stays that way for a day or more.
Caliche is fine dry and slick as ice wet.
Sand is the other way round — often better damp than dry.
After heavy rain, give it a day. The trail will still be there, and so will the ruts you would have cut.

sections.heading: Heat is what catches people out
items: A recovery in August takes hours and you will spend them outside.
A vehicle with no engine running is an oven within minutes. Get into shade, not into the cab.
Water for everyone, and then the amount again. Heat exhaustion in somebody waiting is more likely than an injury during the pull.

sections.heading: What to check before you leave
items: Forecasts and warnings: the National Weather Service, weather.gov.
River and creek levels: the USGS water data site, waterdata.usgs.gov.
Road closures and conditions: TxDOT's DriveTexas, drivetexas.org.
Park closures, burn bans and land rules: Texas Parks and Wildlife, tpwd.texas.gov, and the county you are going to.
Rain that fell fifty miles upstream is the rain that gets you. Look at the whole watershed, not the sky above you.

emergency.title: Emergency contacts
emergency.blurb: Who to call when it is not a job for volunteers.
emergency.lede: Winch Up is neighbours with trucks. Some situations need somebody official, and some need a paid operator with the right machine. These are the numbers, and the point at which to stop waiting and use them.

sections.heading: Call 911 first if any of this is true
items: Somebody is hurt, or might be.
A vehicle is in water, or the water is rising.
You are in or near moving traffic.
There is fuel leaking, smoke, or fire.
Somebody cannot get out of the vehicle.
Nobody on this app is an emergency service. 911 is. Call them first and tell us after.

sections.heading: Stranded on a Texas highway
items: Texas DPS: 1-800-525-5555. Their own wording is to call if your vehicle is disabled or you are stranded on the side of the road, or to report a drunk driver.
Say the road, the direction you were travelling, and the last mile marker or exit you passed. That is what they need first.
Get out on the side away from traffic and stand behind a barrier if there is one. Standing beside a vehicle on a shoulder is how people are killed waiting for help.
Hazard lights on, even in daylight.

sections.heading: Road and weather conditions
items: Texas travel information and emergency road conditions: 1-800-452-9292, daily.
Worth a call before you leave and again if the weather turns. A low-water crossing that was fine this morning is the most common way people here end up needing a recovery.

sections.heading: When you need a paid recovery
items: A wrecker or a winch truck is sometimes the right answer: a rollover, a vehicle well off a road, anything where a strap on a bumper is not going to do it.
If nobody has taken your request after about 25 minutes, your status page shows paid options the admins keep up to date. Nobody on this app is paid, and nobody here takes a cut of that.
Agree the price before anyone hooks up to your vehicle.

sections.heading: On private land or in a park
items: Numbers vary by place and are not listed here. A wrong number at 11pm is worse than no number.
Use the park office or the landowner you got permission from — and if the trail is in our directory, its listing names the source the access was checked against.

emergency.sourceNote: The DPS numbers above were read from the Texas Department of Public Safety travel tips page on 1 October 2026. If one has changed, tell an admin and it will be corrected here.

membership.title: Membership Agreement
membership.intro: Every Winch Up member signs one agreement. It covers asking for help and offering it, because every member can do both.
membership.notPublished: The membership agreement has not been published yet. Nothing is required of you right now, and you can use Winch Up normally.
membership.riskBody: Off-road recovery is dangerous. Winches, straps and chains fail under load and can kill or seriously injure people standing nearby. Volunteers are not a professional towing service, they are not vetted mechanics, and Winch Up does not supervise a recovery or guarantee that anyone will come. By signing, you accept those risks for yourself and your vehicle.

membership.declineHeading: If you would rather not sign
membership.declineBody: You do not have to sign. Without a signature you can still sign in, read the community and change your settings, but you will not be able to request a recovery or offer to help. You can delete your account at any time from your account settings.
membership.consentNote: This agreement is separate from how we contact you. Text messages, email and push notifications are each controlled in your notification settings and are not part of what you are signing here.
membership.requiredBanner: Sign the membership agreement to request a recovery or offer help.

safety.heading: Before you go
safety.requester: Stay with your vehicle if it is safe. Do not stand between a loaded strap and anything it could hit. If anyone is hurt or in the water, call 911 first.
safety.helper: You are volunteering, not being dispatched. Check your gear before you leave, tell someone where you are going, and turn around if the scene is not safe. Nobody at Winch Up expects you to take a risk.

dataDeletion.title: Delete your Winch Up account
dataDeletion.intro: You can delete your account and personal information at any time, from inside the app. This page explains how, and exactly what is removed.
steps: Open the Profile tab, then “Account settings”.
Your account is removed immediately and you are signed out.
dataDeletion.blockedBody: You cannot delete your account while you are in the middle of a recovery — either one you asked for, or one you agreed to help with. Deleting mid-recovery would strand the other person, who may be the one stuck. Cancel or complete it first, then delete.
removedItems: Your name, phone number and email address.
Your profile, your home area and any position you shared.
Your vehicles, your equipment list and any photos of your rig.
dataDeletion.keptWhy: A few records of what happened survive, with your identity removed from them. They no longer name you or point back to you:
keptItems: The record that a recovery took place, with your name, number and exact location stripped out.
Safety and moderation records, so a pattern of harm cannot be erased by deleting an account.
Administrative audit entries, which keep what was done but not who did it.
dataDeletion.noAccessBody: If you have lost access to your account and cannot delete it yourself, email us and we will delete it for you. Write from the address on the account if you can, so we can tell it is you:

adminContent.title: Content & Marketing
adminContent.subtitle: Announcements, events and advertising campaigns, with who each one reaches.
adminContent.categoryHint: Operational means a gate closure, a safety notice, a change to the app. Marketing means anything selling. The difference decides whose consent applies if these are ever sent as notifications.
adminContent.linkHint: Must start with http:// or https://
adminContent.officialNote: An event created here is official. The organiser, website, registration link and contact fields can only be set from this screen — a member posting an event cannot attach them.
adminContent.eventTargetingNote: Targeting an event does not hide it. Every member still sees it in the events list; targeting marks which members it is near, so they can be told about it.
